questions.q: Which animal is known as the King of the Jungle?
questions.exp: Lions are often called the king of the jungle.

questions.q: What do baby kangaroos live in?
questions.exp: A baby kangaroo, called a joey, develops in its mother’s pouch.

questions.q: What do bees make?
questions.exp: Bees make honey from flower nectar.

questions.q: What is a baby dog called?
questions.exp: A young dog is called a puppy.

questions.q: Which animal uses its long trunk to grab food?
questions.exp: An elephant uses its trunk to grasp food and drink water.

questions.q: What sound does a cow make?
questions.exp: Cows are known for their mooing sound.

questions.q: Which animal is often called man’s best friend?
questions.exp: Dogs are famous for being loyal human companions.

questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
questions.exp: A baby cat is a kitten.

questions.q: Which farm animal gives us wool?
questions.exp: Sheep grow wool that can be used for clothing.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for black-and-white stripes?
questions.exp: Zebras have distinctive black-and-white stripe patterns.

questions.q: What do we call a baby cow?
questions.exp: A young cow is called a calf.

questions.q: Which animal says “quack”?
questions.exp: Ducks are known for their quacking sound.

questions.q: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.exp: Kangaroos carry their young in a pouch.

questions.q: What do birds use to fly?
questions.exp: Birds use wings to fly.

questions.q: Which animal is known for changing its colour to blend in?
questions.exp: Chameleons can change colour for camouflage and communication.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.exp: Spiders have eight legs.

questions.q: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
questions.exp: Giraffes are the tallest living land animals.

questions.q: Which bird cannot fly but can run very fast?
questions.exp: Ostriches cannot fly but are excellent runners.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that mainly eats plants?
questions.exp: Herbivores feed mainly on plants.

questions.q: Which reptile is famous for changing its skin colour?
questions.exp: Chameleons are famous for changing colour.

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs?
questions.exp: The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs.

questions.q: What do we call a group of lions?
questions.exp: A group of lions is called a pride.

questions.q: Which big cat has a mane?
questions.exp: Adult male lions usually grow manes.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.exp: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for building dams?
questions.exp: Beavers build dams from branches, mud and other materials.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and animals?
questions.exp: Omnivores eat both plant and animal foods.

questions.q: A caterpillar can change into which insect?
questions.exp: Many caterpillars transform into butterflies.

questions.q: What is the largest land animal?
questions.exp: The African elephant is the largest living land animal.

questions.q: What is a young kangaroo called?
questions.exp: A young kangaroo is called a joey.

questions.q: Which animal is known for a very long neck?
questions.exp: A giraffe’s long neck helps it reach high leaves.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for storing food in its cheeks?
questions.exp: Hamsters can carry food in expandable cheek pouches.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest living bird?
questions.exp: The ostrich is the largest living bird.

questions.q: What is a baby goat called?
questions.exp: A young goat is called a kid.

questions.q: What is a baby horse called?
questions.exp: A young horse is called a foal.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for its black-and-white colouring and lives in Antarctica?
questions.exp: Penguins are flightless birds found in the Southern Hemisphere, especially Antarctica.

questions.q: Which animal has a shell and can move very slowly?
questions.exp: Tortoises have protective shells and generally move slowly.

questions.q: What is a group of fish called?
questions.exp: A group of fish swimming together is called a school.

questions.q: Which animal is known for laughing-like calls?
questions.exp: Some hyena calls sound like laughter.

questions.q: Which animal is known for having a very long tongue and feeding on ants?
questions.exp: Anteaters use their long sticky tongues to collect ants and termites.

questions.q: Which animal can live both in water and on land?
questions.exp: Frogs are amphibians and spend parts of their lives in water and on land.

questions.q: Which animal is known for carrying a shell on its back?
questions.exp: A snail carries its hard shell as protection.

questions.q: Which animal is a marsupial?
questions.exp: Koalas are marsupials and raise their young in pouches.

questions.q: Which animal is known for its long tusks?
questions.exp: Elephants can have long tusks made of ivory.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for building webs?
questions.exp: Spiders build webs to catch prey or provide shelter.

questions.q: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.exp: Dolphins are mammals that breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.q: Which animal is known for its pouch and lives in Australia?
questions.exp: Kangaroos are iconic Australian marsupials.

questions.q: Which animal has a long sticky tongue for catching insects?
questions.exp: Anteaters use long tongues to collect ants and termites.

questions.q: Which animal is known for changing from a tadpole into an adult?
questions.exp: Frogs begin life as tadpoles and undergo metamorphosis.

questions.q: Which animal is a nocturnal mammal that can fly?
questions.exp: Bats are the only mammals capable of sustained true flight.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for its strong memory and large ears?
questions.exp: Elephants have large ears and highly developed memories and social behaviour.

questions.q: Why do mammals such as humans breathe with lungs instead of gills?
questions.exp: Lungs take oxygen from air and remove carbon dioxide.

questions.q: A food chain starts with grass. Which organism is the primary consumer?
questions.exp: A primary consumer eats producers such as grass.

questions.q: Why are polar bears mostly white?
questions.exp: White fur helps polar bears blend into snowy surroundings.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a camel survive long periods with little water?
opts: It stores water in its hump
questions.exp: Camels have adaptations that reduce water loss; the hump stores fat, not water.

questions.q: What is the main role of a predator in an ecosystem?
opts: It hunts other organisms for food
questions.exp: Predators help control populations by feeding on prey.

questions.q: Which statement best describes metamorphosis?
opts: A major change in body form during development
questions.exp: Metamorphosis is a major change in body form during development, as in frogs and butterflies.

questions.q: Why do birds have hollow or lightweight bones?
opts: They help reduce body weight for flight
questions.exp: Many flying birds have lightweight skeletons that help with flight.

questions.q: Which animal relationship is an example of mutualism?
opts: Bees get nectar while flowers are pollinated
A tick feeds on a dog
questions.exp: Both bees and flowering plants benefit from the interaction.

questions.q: If a habitat loses most of its plants, what is likely to happen first to herbivores?
questions.exp: Herbivores depend directly on plants for food.

questions.q: Why do some animals migrate seasonally?
opts: To find food, breeding grounds, or better conditions
questions.exp: Migration can help animals find food, reproduce, or survive seasonal changes.

questions.q: A scientist finds an animal with feathers, a beak and scales on its legs. Which group does it belong to?
questions.exp: Feathers are a defining feature of birds.

questions.q: If all the predators disappeared from an ecosystem, what could happen to prey populations?
opts: They could increase and overuse resources
questions.exp: Without predators, prey numbers can rise and place greater pressure on food and habitats.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly shows the life cycle of a butterfly?
questions.exp: Butterflies develop through four stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa and adult.

questions.q: Why can a whale not be classified as a fish even though it lives in water?
opts: It is a mammal that breathes air and nurses its young
questions.exp: Whales are mammals: they breathe air with lungs and feed milk to their young.

questions.q: Which adaptation would be most useful to an animal hunting at night?
opts: Excellent night vision or other enhanced senses
Very thin fur in a cold climate
questions.exp: Nocturnal animals often have enhanced senses such as night vision, hearing or smell.

questions.q: In a food web, what is most likely to happen if a disease greatly reduces a prey species?
opts: Predators that depend on it may also decline
questions.exp: A major reduction in prey can reduce food available to predators.

questions.q: Which feature most strongly identifies an amphibian rather than a reptile?
opts: A life cycle that commonly includes an aquatic larval stage
questions.exp: Many amphibians begin life in water and later develop adult forms suited to land.

questions.q: Why do elephants use their trunks for more than just drinking?
opts: The trunk can grasp food, spray water and communicate
It is used to lay eggs
questions.exp: The trunk is a highly flexible organ used for feeding, drinking, smelling and communication.

questions.q: What is natural selection most likely to favour in a population?
opts: Inherited traits that improve survival or reproduction in a given environment
Traits chosen by the animal because they look nice
Only traits learned during the animal’s lifetime
questions.exp: Natural selection changes populations when inherited differences affect survival or reproduction.

questions.q: Why can two animals from the same species look slightly different from each other?
opts: They can inherit different combinations of genes
They always have different numbers of chromosomes
Their habitats change their DNA instantly
questions.exp: Genetic variation creates differences among individuals of the same species.

questions.q: A rabbit population becomes isolated from nearby rabbits for many generations. Which process could make it genetically different over time?
opts: Reduced gene flow combined with mutation, selection and drift
questions.exp: Isolation can reduce gene flow and allow populations to diverge.

questions.q: Why can a disease that affects only one prey species still change the abundance of plants in an ecosystem?
opts: Predator numbers and feeding pressure can change through the food web
Diseases always increase plant growth directly
Predators do not depend on prey
questions.exp: Changes can propagate through feeding relationships.

questions.q: A population of rabbits suddenly has many more foxes hunting them. Which change is most likely first?
questions.exp: More predators usually increase prey deaths.

questions.q: Why does a camel’s hump help it survive in a desert?
opts: It stores fat that can be used for energy
It stores a large tank of water
It makes the camel breathe underwater
It keeps the camel from sweating
questions.exp: A hump stores fat, which can be used for energy when food is scarce.

questions.q: A bird has a long, narrow beak that can reach deep into flowers. What is this most likely an adaptation for?
questions.exp: A long narrow beak can help a bird reach nectar that other animals cannot easily reach.

questions.q: Two species both eat the same seeds in one habitat. What relationship are they most likely experiencing?
questions.exp: When organisms depend on the same limited resource, they compete.

questions.q: Why would an animal with thick fur generally struggle more in a very hot environment?
opts: It may have difficulty releasing excess body heat
questions.exp: Thick insulation can make heat loss harder in hot conditions.

questions.q: A grassland loses 80% of its grasses after a long drought. Which sequence is most likely?
opts: Herbivores decline, then predators may decline
Predators increase, then grasses increase immediately
questions.exp: Less plant food can reduce herbivores, which can then reduce food available to predators.

questions.q: In a food web, insects eat plants, frogs eat insects, and snakes eat frogs. If pesticides greatly reduce insects, what is the most likely short-term effect?
opts: Frogs may decrease because less food is available
Frogs immediately increase because there are fewer insects
Plants must decrease because frogs eat plants
Snakes immediately increase because frogs have more food
questions.exp: Removing a major prey source can cause the next consumer level to decline.

questions.q: A biologist finds an animal that is warm-blooded, has hair, produces milk, and lays eggs. Which conclusion is best?
questions.exp: Monotremes are unusual mammals that lay eggs.

questions.q: Why can a small change in one species sometimes affect many other species in a food web?
opts: Species are connected through feeding relationships
Every species eats exactly the same food
questions.exp: A food web contains many linked feeding relationships, so a change can spread through several levels.

questions.q: A population of moths contains mostly pale moths. After tree bark becomes dark from pollution, dark moths survive more often. What does this illustrate?
questions.exp: If inherited traits affect survival and reproduction, natural selection can change population frequencies.

questions.q: Which observation would provide the strongest evidence that two animal species are competing for the same limited resource?
opts: When the resource becomes scarce, both populations show reduced access to it
Both species have the same colour
Both species sleep during the day
questions.exp: Direct evidence of shared use of a limited resource is stronger than similarities in appearance.

questions.q: A parasite population increases inside a host population. Which outcome could occur if the parasite causes serious disease?
opts: Host survival or reproduction may decrease
questions.exp: A harmful parasite can reduce host health, survival, or reproduction.

questions.q: Why are genetic differences within a species important when the environment changes?
opts: Some individuals may have traits that improve survival
All individuals will automatically change their genes
questions.exp: Variation gives natural selection differences to act upon.

questions.q: A frog population is declining because a wetland is drying. Which evidence would best test whether habitat loss is responsible?
opts: Compare frog populations in similar wetlands with different water availability
Count only the number of frog colours
Measure the length of the frogs once
questions.exp: A comparison with similar habitats helps isolate the relationship between water availability and population size.

questions.q: Why can removing a top predator sometimes cause an increase in plant damage?
opts: Its prey may increase and consume more herbivores or other species that affect plants
Plants need predators to make sunlight
Removing predators makes soil instantly fertile
questions.exp: Predator removal can trigger a trophic cascade through the food web.

questions.q: Which combination best describes an adaptation?
opts: A heritable trait that can improve survival or reproduction in a particular environment
A behaviour learned once that changes DNA
questions.exp: Adaptations are inherited characteristics shaped over generations by selection.

questions.q: A scientist observes that a population of finches with deeper beaks survives a drought better because the remaining seeds are hard. What prediction follows?
opts: If the pattern continues, deeper beaks may become more common over generations
Every finch will grow a deeper beak during the drought
The seeds will become softer because of the birds
questions.exp: Differential survival and reproduction can change trait frequencies over generations.

questions.q: Why are decomposers essential to a stable ecosystem?
opts: They return nutrients from dead material to forms other organisms can use
questions.exp: Decomposers recycle nutrients from dead organisms and waste.

questions.q: An animal is active at night, has large eyes, and has highly sensitive hearing. What is the best inference?
opts: These traits may help it find food or avoid danger in low light
The traits prove it is a reptile
questions.exp: Large eyes and sensitive hearing can be useful for nocturnal activity.

questions.q: Why might a species with a very narrow diet be more vulnerable to habitat change than an omnivore?
opts: It may lose its main food source more easily
It can always eat any plant or animal
It does not need a habitat
questions.exp: Specialists may depend heavily on particular resources.

questions.q: A disease kills many individuals of one prey species. Which predator response is most plausible if it depends heavily on that prey?
opts: Its population may later decline because food is scarcer
It will no longer need energy
questions.exp: Predators that rely strongly on a declining prey species can face food shortages.

questions.q: Which evidence would best distinguish camouflage from warning coloration?
opts: Camouflage makes an animal harder to detect, while warning coloration makes it conspicuous to signal danger or unpalatability
Warning coloration only occurs in mammals
Camouflage always means the animal is poisonous
questions.exp: The two strategies have opposite effects on visibility and communicate different survival advantages.

questions.q: Why can island animals evolve differently from closely related mainland animals?
opts: Isolation can reduce gene flow while different environments create different selection pressures
All island animals have identical genes
questions.exp: Geographic isolation can allow populations to diverge over time.

questions.q: A wolf population has inherited variation in coat colour. If one colour survives and reproduces more successfully, which process changes allele frequencies?
questions.exp: Natural selection changes allele frequencies when heritable differences affect reproductive success.

questions.q: Why can a small island population diverge genetically from a mainland population of the same species?
opts: Founder effects and genetic drift can be stronger
questions.exp: Small populations are especially affected by founder effects and genetic drift.

questions.q: A bat and a whale both use sound to locate objects. Their similar echolocation systems are best described as what?
questions.exp: Similar functions can evolve independently; these are analogous adaptations.

questions.q: If an ecosystem loses its apex predator, which change is a plausible trophic cascade?
opts: Prey increase and vegetation may decline
questions.exp: Removing top predators can release prey from predation and alter lower trophic levels.

questions.q: Why does inbreeding increase the chance of a harmful recessive allele being expressed?
opts: Two copies of the same recessive allele are more likely to meet
It creates new recessive alleles instantly
questions.exp: Related individuals are more likely to share the same recessive alleles.

questions.q: A bird has a beak suited to large seeds. A long drought leaves mostly small soft seeds. What could selection favour?
opts: Beaks better suited to the remaining food
Every bird changes its beak during life
questions.exp: Selection can favour heritable traits that improve feeding under changed conditions.

questions.q: Two populations become separated by a canyon, stop exchanging genes, and eventually become reproductively isolated. What process occurred?
questions.exp: Geographic isolation can lead to divergence and reproductive isolation.

questions.q: Which observation most strongly supports directional selection for larger body size?
opts: Average size and associated allele frequencies rise across generations
Every individual grows after eating more
The habitat warms for one day
questions.exp: A heritable population shift across generations indicates evolutionary change.

questions.q: A parasite population becomes drug-resistant and resistant individuals leave more offspring during treatment. What best explains this?
opts: The drug selected among heritable variation for resistance
The drug taught parasites to mutate
Parasites changed genes because they wanted to survive
questions.exp: Selection favours resistant heritable variants when the drug is present.

questions.q: Two equally sized populations face a new disease. Population A has much higher genetic diversity. Why may A be more resilient?
opts: It is more likely to contain variants that confer resistance
questions.exp: Greater variation gives natural selection more possibilities to respond to new conditions.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.exp: Mars looks reddish because of iron-rich dust.

questions.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.exp: The Sun is the star closest to Earth.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.exp: There are eight recognized planets in our solar system.

questions.q: What do astronauts wear to breathe in space?
questions.exp: Spacesuits provide life support in the harsh environment of space.

questions.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.exp: Earth’s rotation causes day and night.

questions.q: What is the name of the space station where astronauts live and work in orbit?
questions.exp: The International Space Station is a laboratory in low Earth orbit.

questions.q: What natural object orbits Earth and shines at night?
questions.exp: The Moon orbits Earth and reflects sunlight.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.exp: Earth is our home planet.

questions.q: What do we call a rocky object from space that reaches Earth’s surface?
questions.exp: A meteorite is a space rock that reaches the ground.

questions.q: What do we call someone who travels into space?
questions.exp: Astronauts are trained to travel and work in space.

questions.q: What shape is Earth approximately?
questions.exp: Earth is approximately spherical.

questions.q: Which planet is the biggest in our solar system?
questions.exp: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.

questions.q: What do we use to look at faraway stars and planets?
questions.exp: Telescopes help us observe distant objects in space.

questions.q: What is the name of the U.S. space agency?
questions.exp: NASA is the United States space agency.

questions.q: What do we call a group of stars that appears to form a pattern?
questions.exp: A constellation is an apparent pattern of stars.

questions.q: What galaxy contains our solar system?
questions.exp: Our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: Which planet has famous visible rings?
questions.exp: Saturn is famous for its extensive ring system.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun?
questions.exp: Earth takes about one year to complete one orbit.

questions.q: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.exp: Gravity attracts objects toward Earth.

questions.q: What is a star explosion called?
questions.exp: A supernova is a powerful stellar explosion.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.exp: Mercury is the innermost planet.

questions.q: What is a huge collection of stars, gas and dust called?
questions.exp: Galaxies contain stars, gas, dust and other matter.

questions.q: What are Saturn’s rings mostly made of?
questions.exp: Saturn’s rings contain mostly ice particles and rocky material.

questions.q: Which planet is similar in size to Earth?
questions.exp: Venus is close to Earth in size.

questions.q: What is a black hole?
opts: A region with gravity so strong light cannot escape
questions.exp: A black hole has an extremely strong gravitational field.

questions.q: What is the path of a planet around a star called?
questions.exp: An orbit is the path one object follows around another.

questions.q: Which animal was the first to orbit Earth?
questions.exp: Laika, a Soviet space dog, was the first animal to orbit Earth.

questions.q: About how long does moonlight take to reach Earth?
questions.exp: Light from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its Great Red Spot?
questions.exp: Jupiter has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.

questions.q: What is Earth’s natural satellite?
questions.exp: The Moon is Earth’s natural satellite.

questions.q: What is a comet mainly made of?
questions.exp: Comets contain ice, dust and rocky material.

questions.q: What do we call a space rock before it enters Earth’s atmosphere?
questions.exp: A meteoroid is a relatively small rocky or metallic body in space.

questions.q: What is a meteor often called when it makes a bright streak in the sky?
questions.exp: A meteor can look like a shooting star as it burns in the atmosphere.

questions.q: Which planet is known for its blue colour and strong winds?
questions.exp: Neptune is a blue ice giant with very fast winds.

questions.q: Which planet has the most prominent ring system?
questions.exp: Saturn’s rings are the most prominent and easily observed.

questions.q: What is the Sun mostly made of?
questions.exp: The Sun is mostly hydrogen and helium.

questions.q: What is the name of our star?
questions.exp: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

questions.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
opts: Changing views of its sunlit side
questions.exp: We see different portions of the Moon’s illuminated half as it orbits Earth.

questions.q: What is the first planet from the Sun?
questions.exp: Mercury is closest to the Sun.

questions.q: What is the fourth planet from the Sun?
questions.exp: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for being very hot because of a thick atmosphere?
questions.exp: Venus has a very thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere and an intense greenhouse effect.

questions.q: What is a light-year used to measure?
questions.exp: A light-year is a unit of distance.

questions.q: What is the Milky Way?
questions.exp: The Milky Way is the galaxy containing our solar system.

questions.q: What do astronauts experience when they appear to float in orbit?
questions.exp: Astronauts in orbit experience microgravity and appear to float.

questions.q: Which object is at the centre of our solar system?
questions.exp: The Sun is at the centre of our solar system.

questions.q: What is the name of the first human-made satellite?
questions.exp: Sputnik 1, launched in 1957, was the first artificial satellite.

questions.q: What does a rocket need to push against to move forward in space?
questions.exp: Rockets move forward by expelling exhaust gases, following Newton’s laws.

questions.q: Which planet is often called the morning or evening star?
questions.exp: Venus is often very bright and visible near sunrise or sunset.

questions.q: What is the Hubble Space Telescope used for?
questions.exp: Hubble observes astronomical objects from space.

questions.q: What is a solar eclipse?
opts: The Moon passes between Earth and the Sun
Earth passes between the Sun and Moon
questions.exp: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon blocks some or all of the Sun from view.

questions.q: Why does the Moon appear to change shape during the month?
opts: We see different portions of its sunlit half
The Moon changes its actual shape
Its light switches on and off
questions.exp: The Moon keeps roughly the same shape, but its position changes how much of its sunlit side we see.

questions.q: Why is a year on Mars longer than a year on Earth?
opts: Mars takes longer to orbit the Sun
questions.exp: A year is the time needed to orbit the Sun, and Mars has a longer orbit.

questions.q: What causes a solar eclipse?
opts: The Moon passes between Earth and the Sun
Earth passes between the Moon and Sun
The Sun passes between Earth and Moon
questions.exp: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon moves between Earth and the Sun.

questions.q: Why do astronauts appear weightless while orbiting Earth?
opts: They and their spacecraft are in continuous free fall around Earth
There is no gravity in space
questions.exp: Astronauts in orbit are continuously falling around Earth, creating the sensation of weightlessness.

questions.q: Which planet has the most prominent ring system?
questions.exp: Saturn is famous for its extensive and bright ring system.

questions.q: What is a light-year used to measure?
questions.exp: A light-year is a unit of distance: how far light travels in one year.

questions.q: Why does the Sun appear brighter than other stars?
opts: It is much closer to Earth
It is the largest star in the universe
It is the only star with light
It is made of solid rock
questions.exp: The Sun is our nearest star, so it appears much brighter than distant stars.

questions.q: What is an orbit?
opts: The path one object follows around another object
questions.exp: An orbit is the path followed by an object under gravity around another object.

questions.q: Which force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.exp: The Sun’s gravity keeps planets moving in their orbits.

questions.q: Why do we have seasons on Earth?
opts: Earth’s tilted axis changes how sunlight is received during its orbit
Earth moves much closer to the Sun every summer
The Moon blocks sunlight in winter
The Sun changes size each season
questions.exp: Earth’s axial tilt causes different parts of Earth to receive sunlight at different angles during the year.

questions.q: A planet has a very dense atmosphere and extreme surface pressure. Which observation would best help compare it with Earth?
opts: Measure the colour of its clouds only
Count how many stars appear nearby
questions.exp: Composition and pressure are key measurements for comparing planetary atmospheres.

questions.q: Why do inner planets generally have shorter years than outer planets?
opts: They travel around the Sun along smaller orbits
questions.exp: Objects closer to the Sun generally have smaller orbital paths and shorter orbital periods.

questions.q: What happens to a star when its core can no longer maintain the reactions that support it?
opts: Its structure can change dramatically as gravity takes over
questions.exp: When internal pressure can no longer balance gravity, a star can undergo major structural changes.

questions.q: Why can’t we see the far side of the Moon from Earth as a normal changing face?
opts: The Moon rotates once in about the same time it orbits Earth
Earth blocks the far side permanently
The far side has no sunlight
questions.exp: The Moon is tidally locked, so its rotation period matches its orbital period around Earth.

questions.q: Which observation is strongest evidence that Earth rotates?
opts: The apparent daily movement of stars across the sky
questions.exp: Earth’s rotation makes stars and the Sun appear to move across our sky each day.

questions.q: Why is a telescope in space often able to produce clearer observations than one on the ground?
opts: It avoids much of Earth’s atmosphere
It is automatically closer to every star
questions.exp: Earth’s atmosphere can blur or absorb some light, while space telescopes avoid that interference.

questions.q: A spacecraft travels farther from Earth. What happens to radio signals between it and Earth?
questions.exp: Radio signals travel at the speed of light, so greater distance means greater travel time.

questions.q: Why do scientists use spectra from stars?
opts: They can reveal information about temperature, motion and chemical composition
They show the exact shape of every planet
questions.exp: Starlight spectra contain clues about a star’s composition, temperature and motion.

questions.q: What is the main reason a black hole is difficult to observe directly?
opts: Its gravity is so strong that light cannot escape from within its event horizon
It is made of invisible water
It is always smaller than an atom
questions.exp: Light cannot escape from inside a black hole’s event horizon, so scientists detect black holes through their effects.

questions.q: If an asteroid’s orbit crosses Earth’s orbit, what is the most important factor in assessing impact risk?
opts: Whether the two objects could reach the same location at the same time
questions.exp: An impact requires the objects to arrive at the same place at the same time, not merely have crossing paths.

questions.q: If Earth suddenly had no atmosphere, which change would be most immediate?
opts: There would be no breathable air at the surface
Earth would stop orbiting the Sun
questions.exp: The atmosphere supplies the gases needed for breathing and affects many surface processes.

questions.q: Why does the Moon have much more obvious craters than Earth?
opts: Earth has erosion and active geology that erase many old craters
Earth is closer to the Sun
questions.exp: Weathering, erosion, oceans and geology continually modify Earth’s surface.

questions.q: A planet takes 400 Earth days to orbit its star. What does that tell you?
opts: Its year is about 400 Earth days long
Its day must also be 400 days
It must be larger than Earth
questions.exp: A year is the time required to complete one orbit.

questions.q: Why can we see stars that are no longer in the same state they are today?
opts: Their light takes time to travel to Earth
Stars stop producing light at night
questions.exp: We observe distant objects through light that may have travelled for years or much longer.

questions.q: If a planet has no natural satellites, which statement is safest?
opts: It simply means no moon has been detected orbiting it
questions.exp: A planet can exist without a natural satellite.

questions.q: Why does observing a distant galaxy allow astronomers to study its past?
opts: Its light needs time to travel across space before reaching us
Stars only exist after we observe them
questions.exp: The farther away an object is, the longer its light has taken to reach us.

questions.q: A star’s spectrum contains dark lines at specific wavelengths. What can astronomers infer from these lines?
opts: The lines can reveal which elements are present
The star must be a planet
The lines prove the star has no gravity
The spectrum tells only its age
questions.exp: Atoms absorb or emit characteristic wavelengths, creating spectral signatures.

questions.q: Why does an astronaut in orbit feel weightless even though Earth’s gravity is still acting strongly?
opts: The astronaut and spacecraft are continuously falling around Earth together
There is no mass in space
The spacecraft is outside Earth’s gravitational field
questions.exp: Orbital motion is continuous free fall around Earth.

questions.q: A planet orbits closer to its star than Earth does. Which is generally expected if the star is similar to the Sun?
opts: The planet completes an orbit in less time
The planet must have no atmosphere
questions.exp: Closer planets generally have shorter orbital periods under the same general gravitational conditions.

questions.q: What would happen to the apparent position of a nearby star if Earth moves to the opposite side of its orbit?
opts: Its position can appear to shift slightly against much more distant stars
The star would physically move instantly
The star would become a planet
questions.exp: This apparent shift is called stellar parallax.

questions.q: Why are radio telescopes useful even though humans cannot see radio waves?
opts: They detect wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation outside visible light
They turn radio waves into gravity
They only work on the Moon
questions.exp: Radio telescopes observe electromagnetic radiation at radio wavelengths.

questions.q: A black hole is difficult to see directly mainly because
opts: Light cannot escape from inside its event horizon
It is made only of empty space
questions.exp: No light escapes from within the event horizon, so the black hole itself is not directly visible.

questions.q: If the Sun were replaced by a star with the same mass but much less brightness, what would happen to Earth’s orbit immediately?
opts: Its orbit would be nearly unchanged by brightness alone
The Moon would leave the Solar System
questions.exp: Orbital motion depends primarily on mass and distance, not visible brightness.

questions.q: Why does a total lunar eclipse occur only when the Sun, Earth and Moon are suitably aligned?
opts: Earth must pass between the Sun and Moon so Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon
The Moon must pass between Earth and the Sun
The Sun must stop producing light
questions.exp: A lunar eclipse requires the Moon to enter Earth’s shadow.

questions.q: What is the strongest reason seasons are not caused simply by Earth being closer to the Sun in summer?
opts: Earth’s axial tilt changes the angle and duration of sunlight received by each hemisphere
The Sun changes size every season
questions.exp: Axial tilt changes solar angle and daylight duration, producing seasons.

questions.q: A spacecraft sends a signal to Earth from a much greater distance. What unavoidable effect increases?
questions.exp: Signals travel at finite speed, so greater distance means longer communication time.

questions.q: Why can a planet with a thick atmosphere have a much hotter surface than expected from its distance from the Sun?
opts: Atmospheric gases can produce a strong greenhouse effect
Thick atmospheres always reflect all sunlight
questions.exp: Greenhouse gases can trap outgoing infrared energy and raise surface temperature.

questions.q: If two stars have the same surface temperature but one appears brighter from Earth, what could explain this?
opts: The brighter-looking star could be much closer or intrinsically more luminous
The dimmer star must have no gravity
The brighter star must be a planet
questions.exp: Apparent brightness depends on intrinsic luminosity and distance.

questions.q: What observation would most strongly support the idea that an exoplanet has an atmosphere?
opts: Spectral features of gases appear in the planet’s transmitted or reflected light
The planet has a circular orbit
The planet is farther away than Earth
questions.exp: Atmospheric gases can leave identifiable spectral signatures.

questions.q: Why is the cosmic microwave background important to cosmology?
opts: It is relic radiation from the early universe and carries information about its early state
It is light from Earth’s atmosphere
It is produced by today’s thunderstorms
It proves every star is the same age
questions.exp: The CMB is leftover radiation from the early hot universe.

questions.q: If a star runs out of hydrogen fuel in its core, what can happen next?
opts: Its core and surrounding layers can change as new fusion stages or collapse processes begin
The star immediately becomes a planet
questions.exp: Changes in core fuel can alter the balance between gravity and pressure and lead to later stellar stages.

questions.q: Why can a planet remain in orbit instead of falling straight into its star?
opts: Its forward motion and the star’s gravity combine to create a curved orbital path
questions.exp: Orbital velocity gives the planet sideways motion while gravity continually curves its path.

questions.q: Which discovery would be strongest evidence of liquid water having existed on Mars in the past?
opts: Mineral deposits and landforms formed by long-lasting water activity
A picture of Mars looking red
Mars being farther from the Sun than Earth
questions.exp: Certain minerals and geological structures can preserve evidence of ancient water.

questions.q: Why do astronomers use different kinds of telescopes, such as infrared and X-ray telescopes?
opts: Different wavelengths reveal different physical processes and objects
All wavelengths carry exactly the same information
Visible light cannot travel through space
X-rays are easier for human eyes to see
questions.exp: Different wavelengths reveal different temperatures, materials and energetic processes.

questions.q: A galaxy’s spectral lines are shifted toward longer wavelengths. What can this indicate?
opts: The galaxy is moving away from us relative to the observer
The galaxy has stopped producing light
questions.exp: A redshift can indicate recession due to relative motion and, on cosmic scales, expansion.

questions.q: Why does an astronaut in orbit appear weightless while Earth's gravity still acts strongly?
opts: The astronaut and spacecraft are continuously falling around Earth together
There is no gravity above the atmosphere
questions.exp: Orbit is continuous free fall; gravity provides the centripetal acceleration.

questions.q: A planet has Earth's radius but twice Earth's mass. Ignoring rotation, what happens to surface gravity?
questions.exp: Surface gravity is proportional to mass divided by radius squared.

questions.q: Why can a planet farther from its star have a longer orbital period?
opts: It generally follows a larger orbit and has a lower average orbital speed
questions.exp: Kepler's laws relate larger orbital size to longer orbital periods.

questions.q: What does a stellar absorption spectrum reveal most directly?
opts: Which elements are present in the star's atmosphere
The star's age to the nearest day
questions.exp: Elements absorb characteristic wavelengths, producing identifiable spectral lines.

questions.q: Two stars have the same apparent brightness, but one is much farther away. What must generally be true of the distant one?
questions.exp: Brightness decreases with distance squared, so a farther star must be more luminous to appear equally bright.

questions.q: Why is axial tilt important for seasons on an Earth-like planet?
opts: It changes the angle and duration of incoming sunlight through the orbit
It changes distance from the star to zero
questions.exp: Tilt changes solar angle and daylight duration through the year.

questions.q: A galaxy's spectral lines are redshifted relative to laboratory lines. What is the common cosmological interpretation?
opts: The galaxy is receding relative to us as space expands
The galaxy is inside the Solar System
questions.exp: Cosmological redshift is associated with expansion and increased wavelength.

questions.q: Why is the cosmic microwave background important to cosmology?
opts: It is relic radiation from the early universe that constrains models of its evolution
It proves all galaxies are the same age
It is caused by radio stations
questions.exp: The CMB is a major source of evidence about the early universe.

questions.q: Which process is associated with producing many very heavy elements in extreme astrophysical environments?
questions.exp: Rapid neutron capture in events such as neutron-star mergers can build very heavy nuclei.

questions.q: Why is detecting both a planetary transit and radial-velocity signal especially useful?
opts: Transit constrains radius while radial velocity helps constrain mass
questions.exp: The two methods provide complementary size and mass information.

questions.q: What is the biggest animal in the ocean?
questions.exp: Blue whales are the largest animals known to have lived.

questions.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.exp: An octopus has eight arms.

questions.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
questions.exp: Gills extract oxygen from water.

questions.q: What is a group of fish called?
questions.exp: Fish swimming together form a school.

questions.q: How many arms does a typical starfish have?
questions.exp: Many starfish have five arms.

questions.q: Which ocean animal is a top predator with sharp teeth?
questions.exp: Many shark species are important ocean predators.

questions.q: Which animal has a hard shell and can pull its head inside?
questions.exp: Turtles have protective shells.

questions.q: What colour does ocean water often appear?
questions.exp: Water absorbs and scatters light in ways that often make the ocean look blue.

questions.q: Which sea animal is intelligent and often jumps from the water?
questions.exp: Dolphins are intelligent marine mammals.

questions.q: Which creature has pinchers and often walks sideways?
questions.exp: Crabs commonly move sideways.

questions.q: What do sea turtles come onto beaches to do?
questions.exp: Female sea turtles come ashore to lay eggs.

questions.q: Which sea creature is known for its sting and soft body?
questions.exp: Jellyfish can have stinging cells in their tentacles.

questions.q: What is a baby fish called?
questions.exp: A young fish is called a fry.

questions.q: Which orange-and-white fish lives with sea anemones?
questions.exp: Clownfish often live among sea anemone tentacles.

questions.q: Which creature can regrow a lost arm?
questions.exp: Many starfish can regenerate lost arms.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean?
questions.exp: The Pacific is the largest ocean.

questions.q: Which animal borrows empty shells for protection?
questions.exp: Hermit crabs use empty shells as portable homes.

questions.q: What do dolphins use to locate objects underwater?
questions.exp: Dolphins use echolocation by producing and listening for sound echoes.

questions.q: What are coral reefs built by?
questions.exp: Corals are colonies of tiny animals called polyps.

questions.q: What is a group of dolphins called?
questions.exp: A group of dolphins is called a pod.

questions.q: Which deep ocean zone receives no sunlight?
questions.exp: The midnight zone is too deep for sunlight to reach.

questions.q: What is the biggest fish?
questions.exp: The whale shark is the largest fish species.

questions.q: Which sea creature has three hearts?
questions.exp: An octopus has three hearts.

questions.q: What is the study of oceans called?
questions.exp: Oceanography is the scientific study of oceans.

questions.q: Which ocean zone is exposed at low tide?
questions.exp: The intertidal zone is covered and uncovered by tides.

questions.q: About what percentage of Earth is covered by ocean?
questions.exp: Oceans cover roughly 71% of Earth’s surface.

questions.q: Which marine mammal breathes through a blowhole?
questions.exp: Whales breathe air through blowholes.

questions.q: What is a baby seal called?
questions.exp: A young seal is called a pup.

questions.q: Which sea animal has eight arms and no bones?
questions.exp: Octopuses are soft-bodied animals with eight arms.

questions.q: What do whales breathe?
questions.exp: Whales are mammals and must breathe air.

questions.q: What is seaweed?
questions.exp: Seaweeds are large marine algae.

questions.q: Which animal is known for a hard outer shell and two large claws?
questions.exp: Lobsters have hard exoskeletons and large claws.

questions.q: What is the main source of energy for most ocean food webs?
questions.exp: Sunlight powers photosynthesis in marine plants and algae.

questions.q: Which tiny organisms drift in the ocean and form the base of many food webs?
questions.exp: Plankton are tiny drifting organisms important to ocean food webs.

questions.q: What is a coral reef?
opts: A structure built by coral organisms
questions.exp: Coral organisms build reef structures over time.

questions.q: Which ocean is between Africa and Australia?
questions.exp: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia and Australia.

questions.q: Which ocean lies between Africa and the Americas?
questions.exp: The Atlantic Ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.

questions.q: What causes ocean tides mainly?
opts: The gravity of the Moon and Sun
questions.exp: Tides are mainly caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for changing colour and texture underwater?
questions.exp: Octopuses can change colour and skin texture for camouflage and communication.

questions.q: What is a mangrove?
questions.exp: Mangroves are trees and shrubs adapted to salty coastal environments.

questions.q: Which ocean is the smallest?
questions.exp: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the five recognized oceans.

questions.q: What do sea anemones use to catch prey?
questions.exp: Sea anemones use stinging cells on their tentacles.

questions.q: Which animal is known for producing pearls?
questions.exp: Some oysters and other mollusks can produce pearls.

questions.q: What is an estuary?
opts: A place where fresh and salt water mix
questions.exp: Estuaries form where rivers meet the sea and fresh and salt water mix.

questions.q: What is a kelp forest?
opts: An underwater ecosystem dominated by large algae
questions.exp: Kelp forests are underwater habitats formed by large brown algae.

questions.q: Which animal is known for a long tusk and lives in Arctic waters?
questions.exp: Narwhals are Arctic whales known for their long tusks.

questions.q: What is the deepest known ocean trench called?
questions.exp: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known ocean trench.

questions.q: Which fish is famous for living in clownfish partnerships?
questions.exp: Clownfish live in close association with sea anemones.

questions.q: What is bioluminescence?
questions.exp: Bioluminescence is the production of light by a living organism.

questions.q: Which ocean animal is known for a hard shell and slow movement?
questions.exp: Sea turtles have protective shells and move relatively slowly on land.

questions.q: Why is most deep ocean water very cold?
opts: Sunlight warms mainly the surface, while deep water receives little direct solar energy
Deep water is closer to the Sun
questions.exp: Sunlight penetrates only the upper ocean, so deep water remains much colder.

questions.q: What is the main source of energy for most ocean surface ecosystems?
questions.exp: Phytoplankton use sunlight to make food, supporting many marine food webs.

questions.q: Why are coral reefs often found in warm, shallow seas?
opts: Their coral-building organisms need suitable light and water conditions
questions.exp: Many reef-building corals depend on symbiotic algae that require light.

questions.q: What is an estuary?
opts: A place where freshwater meets and mixes with seawater
questions.exp: Estuaries form where rivers or streams meet the sea and their waters mix.

questions.q: Why are mangrove forests important to coastal areas?
opts: They provide habitat and help protect shorelines
They remove every fish from shallow water
questions.exp: Mangroves shelter wildlife and can reduce erosion and wave energy.

questions.q: What causes ocean tides mainly?
opts: The gravitational pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun
questions.exp: Tides are driven mainly by lunar gravity, with solar gravity also contributing.

questions.q: Why can a whale stay underwater for a long time despite breathing air?
opts: It stores oxygen efficiently and slows its metabolism during dives
questions.exp: Whales store oxygen in blood and muscles and can reduce activity during dives.

questions.q: Which ocean zone receives enough sunlight for photosynthesis?
questions.exp: The photic zone is the sunlit upper layer where photosynthesis can occur.

questions.q: Why does salt water generally have a higher density than fresh water?
opts: Dissolved salts add mass without greatly increasing volume
questions.exp: Dissolved salts increase the mass of a given volume of water.

questions.q: What role do decomposers play in marine ecosystems?
opts: They break down dead material and recycle nutrients
questions.exp: Decomposers help return nutrients from dead organisms to the ecosystem.

questions.q: Why can warmer ocean water contribute to coral bleaching?
opts: Heat can stress corals and cause them to lose their symbiotic algae
Warm water turns coral into fish
questions.exp: High temperatures can stress corals and cause them to expel symbiotic algae, leading to bleaching.

questions.q: If a predator is removed from a marine food web, what is a likely first effect?
questions.exp: Removing a predator can allow some prey populations to grow, changing other parts of the food web.

questions.q: Why do deep-sea animals often have adaptations for very high pressure?
opts: Water pressure increases greatly with depth
The Sun heats deep water strongly
questions.exp: Pressure increases with depth, so deep-sea organisms need structures and behaviours suited to it.

questions.q: How can upwelling increase fish populations near some coasts?
opts: It brings nutrient-rich deep water toward the surface
It removes oxygen from all fish
questions.exp: Upwelling supplies nutrients that can increase plankton and support larger food webs.

questions.q: Why are phytoplankton important to the global carbon cycle?
opts: They use carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and form the base of many food webs
They live only on the seafloor
questions.exp: Phytoplankton take up carbon dioxide through photosynthesis and support marine food webs.

questions.q: What is the thermocline?
opts: A layer where temperature changes rapidly with depth
questions.exp: The thermocline is a region where water temperature decreases rapidly with depth.

questions.q: Why can oil spills be especially harmful to seabirds?
opts: Oil can coat feathers and reduce insulation and waterproofing
questions.exp: Oil damages feather waterproofing and insulation, making it harder for birds to stay warm and survive.

questions.q: Why does sound travel differently underwater than in air?
opts: Water has different physical properties that change sound speed and transmission
questions.exp: Sound travels faster and behaves differently in water because water’s density and elasticity differ from air.

questions.q: A coral reef loses many herbivorous fish. What could happen if algae then grow unchecked?
opts: Algae can compete with corals for space and light
questions.exp: Herbivorous fish help control algae; too much algae can reduce coral growth and recruitment.

questions.q: Why can melting land ice raise sea level more directly than melting floating sea ice?
opts: Land ice adds new water to the ocean when it melts
Floating ice is heavier than seawater
questions.exp: Melting ice already floating in seawater has little direct effect on sea level, while land ice adds water to the ocean.

questions.q: Why can removing filter-feeding organisms change water clarity in some coastal ecosystems?
opts: Fewer organisms may remove suspended particles from the water
Water becomes less dense because animals disappear
questions.exp: Filter feeders can remove suspended material and influence water clarity.

questions.q: A deep-sea fish is brought rapidly to the surface. Why might the pressure change be dangerous?
opts: Its tissues and gas-filled structures may not adjust safely to the rapid pressure decrease
questions.exp: Rapid decompression can damage organisms adapted to high pressure.

questions.q: Why is dissolved oxygen important to many fish?
opts: They use it for cellular respiration
They use it to make sunlight
questions.exp: Many aquatic animals need dissolved oxygen for respiration.

questions.q: Why can a coral reef be harmed when seawater becomes unusually warm for too long?
opts: Corals can lose their symbiotic algae and bleach
The reef becomes a freshwater lake
questions.exp: Heat stress can cause corals to expel their symbiotic algae.

questions.q: Why does a deep-sea animal experience enormous pressure?
opts: The weight of the water above it is very large
questions.exp: Pressure increases with depth because of the weight of water above.

questions.q: Why is upwelling often linked with productive fisheries?
opts: It can bring nutrient-rich deep water toward the surface
It removes all nutrients from the ocean
questions.exp: Nutrients brought upward can support phytoplankton and larger food webs.

questions.q: Why do some fish have streamlined bodies?
opts: A streamlined shape can reduce resistance while swimming
It prevents them from using oxygen
It lets them live without water
questions.exp: Streamlining can reduce drag in water.

questions.q: A coastal region experiences strong seasonal upwelling. Why might fish catches increase there?
opts: Nutrients rise into sunlit water, supporting phytoplankton and a larger food web
Fish are pushed upward by sunlight
questions.exp: Nutrient-rich water can stimulate primary production and support more consumers.

questions.q: Why can melting a large glacier on land raise sea level more directly than melting an equal volume of floating sea ice?
opts: Land ice adds new water to the ocean, while floating ice already displaces water
Sea ice is outside Earth’s gravity
questions.exp: Adding land-based meltwater increases ocean volume; floating ice already displaces water.

questions.q: If phytoplankton populations suddenly collapsed across a large ocean region, which effect would be most concerning?
opts: Reduced food supply for organisms that depend on them and reduced carbon uptake
Immediate growth of all fish populations
The ocean would stop having tides
questions.exp: Phytoplankton are major primary producers and important in carbon cycling.

questions.q: Why does sound generally travel faster in seawater than in air?
opts: Water’s physical properties allow pressure disturbances to travel faster through it
questions.exp: Sound speed depends on the medium’s elasticity and density; it is faster in water than air.

questions.q: A marine food web loses most of its large predatory fish. What is a possible trophic cascade?
opts: Some prey populations may rise and then alter lower levels of the food web
questions.exp: Removing predators can allow prey to increase, producing cascading effects.

questions.q: Why are hydrothermal vents able to support ecosystems without sunlight?
opts: Chemosynthetic microbes use chemical energy from vent fluids
Sunlight is stronger at the seafloor
questions.exp: Some microbes obtain energy by oxidising chemicals rather than using sunlight.

questions.q: What is the thermocline?
opts: A layer where water temperature changes rapidly with depth
questions.exp: The thermocline is a zone of rapid temperature change with depth.

questions.q: Why can excess fertiliser runoff cause fish kills in coastal waters?
opts: Nutrient enrichment can fuel algal blooms whose decay consumes dissolved oxygen
Algae always produce too much oxygen at night
questions.exp: Decomposition of excess organic matter can lower oxygen and create hypoxic conditions.

questions.q: Why can mangrove roots reduce damage from waves and storms?
opts: Dense roots can slow water movement and trap sediment
Their leaves turn waves into freshwater
questions.exp: Mangrove root systems can dissipate wave energy and stabilize sediment.

questions.q: Why is the open ocean often less productive per unit area than a nutrient-rich coastal upwelling zone?
opts: Deep nutrients may be far from the sunlit surface where phytoplankton can use them
The open ocean has no sunlight
questions.exp: Nutrients and light availability strongly influence marine primary production.

questions.q: If ocean acidity increases, why can organisms that build calcium carbonate shells or skeletons be affected?
opts: More acidic conditions can make carbonate chemistry less favourable for calcification
Acidification makes all shells instantly stronger
questions.exp: Ocean acidification alters carbonate chemistry and can make calcification harder for some organisms.

questions.q: Why does a whale need to surface even though it lives in the ocean?
opts: It is a mammal and must breathe atmospheric oxygen with lungs
Whales have gills that stop working underwater
questions.exp: Whales breathe air with lungs.

questions.q: What makes a keystone species especially important?
opts: Its effect on an ecosystem can be much larger than expected from its abundance
It is always the largest animal
It never interacts with other species
questions.exp: Keystone species can have disproportionately large ecological effects.

questions.q: Why can a dead zone form after nutrient pollution enters a coastal ecosystem?
opts: Excess nutrients can increase organic matter whose decomposition consumes oxygen
Fish consume all oxygen directly in minutes
questions.exp: Decomposition of excess biomass can consume dissolved oxygen.

questions.q: Why are deep-ocean currents important to Earth’s climate system?
opts: They redistribute heat and dissolved substances around the global ocean
questions.exp: Large-scale ocean circulation transports heat and materials.

questions.q: Why can plastic pollution harm marine animals even when the plastic is not poisonous?
opts: Animals may become entangled or ingest pieces that block or damage their digestive systems
Animals cannot interact with floating objects
questions.exp: Physical entanglement and ingestion are major hazards of marine debris.

questions.q: Why do many deep-sea animals have slow growth or low reproductive rates?
opts: Scarce food and stable but harsh conditions can favour energy-efficient life strategies
questions.exp: Many deep-sea environments have limited food, favouring energy conservation in some species.

questions.q: What would most likely happen if a large seagrass meadow disappeared?
opts: Habitat for juvenile fish and other organisms could decline and sediment may become less stable
The ocean would lose all tides
questions.exp: Seagrass meadows provide habitat and help stabilize sediments.

questions.q: Why does cold, salty seawater tend to sink?
opts: Its density is greater than that of surrounding water
Cold water has no dissolved gas
questions.exp: Temperature and salinity both affect seawater density.

questions.q: What is a major biological consequence of ocean upwelling?
opts: Nutrient-rich deep water reaches the surface and can support high productivity
questions.exp: Upwelling supplies nutrients to sunlit surface waters.

questions.q: Why can excessive nutrient runoff cause coastal fish kills?
opts: Algal blooms can be followed by decomposition that consumes dissolved oxygen
questions.exp: Decomposition can consume oxygen and create hypoxic conditions.

questions.q: Why is coral bleaching dangerous to a coral colony?
opts: The coral loses a major energy source and may die if stress persists
questions.exp: Symbiotic algae provide much of a coral's energy.

questions.q: Why does increasing atmospheric CO₂ tend to make seawater more acidic?
opts: Dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid and alters carbonate chemistry
CO₂ turns salt directly into acid
questions.exp: CO₂ dissolves and shifts the seawater carbonate equilibrium.

questions.q: Why are mangroves important to coastal ecosystems?
opts: They provide habitat, trap sediment and can reduce wave energy and erosion
questions.exp: Mangroves support biodiversity and buffer some coastal impacts.

questions.q: A deep-sea animal produces light through a chemical reaction. What is this called?
questions.exp: Bioluminescence is biologically produced light.

questions.q: Why can a thermocline affect where marine organisms live?
opts: It marks a strong temperature gradient that can separate water masses and affect nutrients and habitat
questions.exp: Strong temperature gradients influence mixing and biological conditions.

questions.q: If most large predators disappear from a marine food web, what long-term effect is plausible?
opts: Mesopredators or herbivores may increase and alter lower trophic levels
questions.exp: Predator removal can trigger trophic cascades.

questions.q: Why can ocean warming raise sea level without adding water from melting ice?
opts: Warmer seawater expands and occupies more volume
questions.exp: Thermal expansion contributes to sea-level rise.

questions.q: How many centimetres are in one metre?

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a square with side 3 cm?
questions.exp: Perimeter is four times the side length.

questions.q: What is 25% of 20?

questions.q: Which number is prime?
questions.exp: Seven has exactly two positive factors: one and seven.

questions.q: What is the next number: 5, 10, 15, 20, __?
questions.exp: The pattern adds five each time.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a full turn?

One thousand plus five hundred is 1,500.

questions.q: Which is greater: 0.8 or 0.6?

questions.q: What is the smallest three-digit number?
questions.exp: 100 is the first three-digit whole number.

questions.q: How many quarters make one whole?
questions.exp: Four quarters make one whole.

questions.q: What is 50 ÷ 5?
questions.exp: Fifty divided by five is ten.

questions.q: Why can mountains cause heavy rain on one side and drier conditions on the other?
opts: Rising air cools and loses moisture, creating a rain-shadow effect
The Sun shines only on one side
questions.exp: Air rising over mountains can cool and release moisture, leaving the other side drier.

questions.q: Which geographic factor most directly explains why coastal areas often have smaller temperature ranges than inland areas?
opts: Water heats and cools more slowly than land
questions.exp: Water changes temperature more slowly than land, moderating nearby temperatures.

questions.q: If a river is polluted upstream, why can communities far downstream be affected?

questions.q: Why are contour lines useful on a physical map?

The process of turning cities into farms

questions.q: Why can a place near the equator receive strong sunlight throughout the year?

It is always closer to the Moon
It is at the North Pole
